relatedSnapshot.title: Investigate: cold email campaign "Built for Success-Saas" (Name 8) shows no emails sent for two days after manual toggle, despite Active status and connected inboxes
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>
Intercom conversation id: 21547599575186

## Claim (testable)

A cold email customer reports that the campaign "Built for Success-Saas" (workspace <workspace-slug>) stopped sending emails for two days after the campaign was toggled from automatic back on, even though the campaign shows Active, 9 inboxes are connected, and enough leads are uploaded; the same page also reports 4,928 leads skipped during upload. Hypothesis to verifying stage: the campaign's own daily send limits (daily_limit / daily_max_leads) were zeroed by the even-split planner during the 2026-09-17 pause/resume while a second campaign existed in the workspace, and no send window has elapsed since, so the campaign reports Active but cannot send.

## Bounded conversation context

* 2026-09-18 (customer, first message): "Help! None of no emails went out in my campaign and I don't know why." Campaign link: Built for Success-Saas.
* Customer follow-up: "My campaign was turned off because I had it set to automatic, and now that I turned it back on, no emails have been sent from the campaign for the past two days"; campaign shows the email addresses, is active, and has enough leads uploaded.
* Customer: "It says 4,928 leads were skipped during upload, 5 on the do not contact list. I need help ... It needs to be running by Monday."
* Fin AI answered with generic checks (campaign status, sending schedule, inboxes) and escalated to a human; a teammate acknowledged.

## Requested follow-up

Confirm the cause, record the blast radius from current production data, identify the first divergent hop if the campaign limits are not the cause, and provide the exact unblock (which field a human must correct and its value). The customer needs the campaign sending before Monday.

relatedSnapshot.title: One-off recovery: backfill + AI SDR replay for the webhook-outage cohort (99 + 207)
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Reopened 2026-06-23 per James (Slack P0 thread) — this is the live one-off recovery run for the webhook-outage cohort.** Previous cancellation reversed so the resync → backfill → AI-SDR-replay is tracked on record (not just in-flight Slack work).

## Problem

During the silent webhook outages, prospect replies arrived while webhooks were down. We've resynced + backfilled most affected workspaces but have NOT re-run AI SDR on those imported replies — importing does not trigger AI SDR (verified in code) — so prospects sit un-answered. Several clients have had this for a couple of weeks and think their campaigns aren't working.

Cohorts: 99 (May-20) resynced+backfilled, not replayed; 207 active-campaign silent dropouts (158 resynced+backfilled, ~49 pending resync, none replayed); plus the two named system-provisioned workspaces `<workspace-slug>` and `<workspace-slug>` (whose admin "resync" never actually re-registered — confirmed via Inngest: no resync run fired).

## Plan (one-off scripts; reuse existing primitives; no new app code)

Strictly ordered, with wait points (ordering is load-bearing):

0. **Detect** — read-only script: active Company One provider + ≥1 active campaign + 0 `outreach_webhook_event` in last N days → org-id list. Confirm count ≈ cohort and that the two named workspaces appear.
1. **Re-register** — fire `OUTREACH_EVENTS.RESYNC_WEBHOOKS` per org (batched; `processResyncWebhook` caps concurrency at 5; uses the shipped create-then-swap from PR #4945). Wait for completion.
2. **Backfill (windowed)** — `OUTREACH_EVENTS.EMAIL_THREADS_BULK_IMPORT` `{ organizationIds, userId: <superadmin>, classifyInterest: true }`. Wait for completion.
3. **Replay** — select positive / last-from-prospect / non-human-owned / non-terminal threads → `admin.sdrReplay.replayThreads` in ≤300-id batches (re-verifies prospect-sent-last before firing).

Depends on PR #4945 (the safe-resync prerequisite). Every driver script ships with a `--dry-run`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All affected orgs (99 + 207 + the 2 named) re-registered and confirmed delivering.
- [ ] Missed messages backfilled (windowed to the silent period; no full-history walk).
- [ ] AI SDR replayed on unanswered prospect threads; no double-replies (idempotency/guards respected).
- [ ] Never replays human-owned (`controlLevel` in human_takeover/dnc/paused/escalated) or terminal-lifecycle (booked/completed/declined) threads.
- [ ] Per-phase structured summary (orgs resynced, threads imported, replays fired/skipped/failed).

Name 9 this flow (auto on every future reconnect) → ENG-10710. Detection / zombie webhooks → ENG-10661 + ENG-10711.

relatedSnapshot.title: Route triage and billing decisions through Jev; Foreman acts on them
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Goal

Every triage and billing judgment Foreman makes goes through Jev (TypeSafe's decision model). Code turns Jev's answers into routing, and Foreman carries that routing out. This is the first step of the Foreman overhaul under ENG-14060. Name 25 tickets from ENG-13999 will later come in through Name 24 intake and use the same decisions.

## Scope

* A Jev client through the company Vercel AI Gateway (`typesafe-ai/jev`, `/v1/evaluate`), restricted to TypeSafe as the provider. It authenticates with the gateway key, or the deployment's OIDC token when no key is set. It does not use the personal TypeSafe account.
* One file holding every question and threshold (`agent/lib/jev-decisions.ts`). Each decision asks all its questions in one batched call. Counts, dates, and "does the evidence exist" checks stay in code.
* Three tools:
  * `classify_ask`: money or product, the billing bucket, and the source labels.
  * `decide_triage`: the Stage 5 verdict, classification, duplicate, handling path, state, priority, labels, and project.
  * `decide_billing`: the discretion note, the 7-item checklist, and the Support/Financial routing.
* Skill wiring:
  * triage-investigate
  * triage-handling and its critic adjudication
  * billing-triage
  * intercom-billing-triage
  * intercom-triage-investigate (lane choice only)
* If Jev can't answer, the skills fall back to the written rules and say so in the document.

## Out of scope

* Jev choosing which evidence lanes to run.
* Code-side enforcement that `route_ticket` matches the decision.
* Name 24 intake context (H1 to H3).
* The ENG-13999 widget moving to the gateway.

## Acceptance

* `pnpm validate` passes.
* A live gateway call with the TypeSafe-only restriction succeeds.
* Aaron has accepted or changed the threshold choices listed in the PR.
* One real triage ticket and one billing ticket run end to end on production, with the routing matching what the prose rules would have given.
